deep.reconstruction:
Title: 'Vortrag des Newtonschen Lehrsatzes über die Summen der Potenzen der Wurzeln der Gleichungen', meaning a presentation of Newton's theorem on the power sums of the roots of equations. The page reads as an outline for teaching. It starts the derivation, and the derivation is finished on the next page (steps 6–10).

(1) Let f(x) = x^m + P x^{m-1} + Q x^{m-2} + R x^{m-3} + ... + T x + U have roots α, β, γ, δ, .... Then f(x) = (x-α)(x-β)(x-γ)(x-δ)···.

(2) This is only stated as a heading: the connection between the coefficients and the roots (Vieta). In modern form: P = -e1, Q = e2, R = -e3, ..., U = (-1)^m e_m, where e_k are the elementary symmetric functions of the roots.

(3) Reversed polynomial. Substitute x = 1/t and multiply by t^m (this justification is mine; Gauss just says 'Man hat dann auch'). This gives
Z(t) := 1 + P t + Q t^2 + R t^3 + ... + T t^{m-1} + U t^m = (1-αt)(1-βt)(1-γt)(1-δt)···.

(4) Difference of Z at two points t and u:
Z(t) - Z(u) = (t-u)[P + Q(t+u) + R(t^2+tu+u^2) + ... + U(t^{m-1}+t^{m-2}u+...+u^{m-1})].
This uses t^k - u^k = (t-u)(t^{k-1}+...+u^{k-1}).

(5) The same difference computed from the product form by telescoping:
∏_i(1-α_i t) - ∏_i(1-α_i u) = Σ_k [∏_{i<k}(1-α_i u)]·[(1-α_k t)-(1-α_k u)]·[∏_{i>k}(1-α_i t)].
Since (1-α_k t)-(1-α_k u) = α_k(u-t), this equals
(u-t)α(1-βt)(1-γt)(1-δt)··· + (u-t)β(1-αu)(1-γt)(1-δt)··· + (u-t)γ(1-αu)(1-βu)(1-δt)··· + (u-t)δ(1-αu)(1-βu)(1-γu)··· + ...

Purpose, completed on the next page:
- Equate (4) and (5) and divide by (t-u).
- Set u = t. This gives Z'(t) = -Σ α Z/(1-αt), i.e. the logarithmic derivative Z'/Z = -Σ α/(1-αt), obtained purely algebraically through difference quotients without calculus.
- Expand each α/(1-αt) as a geometric series and compare coefficients of t^{k-1}.
- Result: Newton's identities S_k + P S_{k-1} + Q S_{k-2} + ... + k·(k-th coefficient) = 0, where S_k = Σ α^k.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page. Steps (3), (4) and (5) are all correct identities.
Step (3) asserts the reversed-polynomial identity without justification; it follows from t^m f(1/t). This is a minor gap, acceptable in a lecture outline.
Step (2) is only a heading; the Vieta relations are not written out.
In step (3) the first factor appears to have been corrected (overwritten) from '1+αt' to '1-αt'. The final reading '1-αt' is correct.
On the next page the last coefficient is called V instead of U, and the term 'mV' should be 'mU t^{m-1}'. These are slips there, not on this page.

results.what: Polynomial as product of linear factors over its roots, plus Vieta's relations between coefficients and roots

results.modern_name: Reversed polynomial / generating function of elementary symmetric functions

results.what: Telescoping difference of two products and the difference quotient of a polynomial, used to obtain the logarithmic derivative algebraically without calculus
results.modern_name: Finite-difference / formal derivative proof of Newton's identities
results.usually_credited_to: variants in Euler, Lagrange and 18th-century algebra textbooks; standard

results.what: Newton's theorem on power sums of roots (target of the derivation, completed on next page)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine lecture-style derivation of Newton's identities, a well-known classical result. The only mildly distinctive feature is that the derivative is avoided by using difference quotients and telescoping, a known textbook technique. It is pedagogical material, not new mathematics.
